guidance: A drill-planning aid, not a measurement: the step lengths are the published plan definitions measured heel to heel, and the times assume the band steps once per count at a steady tempo.
method: Every plan is a definition, not an estimate: N-to-5 means N equal heel-to-heel steps to cover 5 yards, so the step length is 180 divided by N inches - 22.5 for 8-to-5, 30 for 6-to-5, 15 for 12-to-5 and 11.25 for 16-to-5, with 16-to-5 exactly half of 8-to-5. A count is one step when the band steps on every count, which is how drill is normally written, so the distance in inches is the step length times the counts. Time on the field is counts times 60 divided by the tempo in counts per minute, and ground speed in inches per second is the step length times the tempo divided by 60. The page converts that speed to feet per second, miles per hour (3600/63,360) and kilometres per hour (0.0254 m per inch times 3.6). The rank interval multiplies the step length by the number of steps between ranks and prints the result in inches, feet and inches, and metres. Field spans use the playing field between the goal lines, 100 yards long and 53 1/3 yards (160 feet) wide, so at 22.5 inches a marcher needs exactly 160 counts to cover the length and 86 whole counts to cross the width, where 1920/22.5 is 85.33; because a drill count is a whole step, that column rounds up to the next whole count and is labelled whole counts. Display values round half away from zero at two decimals, and a duration of 60 seconds or more also prints as minutes and seconds; the step itself is exact for the four plans, since 180/6, 180/8, 180/12 and 180/16 are terminating values, and no displayed value feeds another calculation. The page does not model diagonals, obliques or jazz running, where the physical step differs from the plan; it does not know a band's individual stride or the tempo of a recording; and it does not treat a count as a note value, which is why a move held in half notes needs its steps entered rather than its note count. Everything runs in the browser.
